bugs.error_message: No way for the shared upstream-ui to look up a user's own per-project role without admin access; also get_current_user's dev-mode bypass ignored TAPIS_ENFORCE_AUTH_IN_DEV unlike authenticate_user
bugs.root_cause: GET /user-roles (list) is admin-gated (get_admin_user) with no self-lookup alternative, so the frontend's multi-project dropdown had no legitimate way to resolve 'what's my role here' per discovered project — this is what led to InstanceContext.tsx hardcoding permission: 'ADMIN' (see upstream-ui bug-001). Separately, get_current_user's `if settings.ENV == 'dev'` bypass returned a fake ADMIN user with zero token check, inconsistent with authenticate_user which already respected TAPIS_ENFORCE_AUTH_IN_DEV for the same purpose — flagged by security review as higher-risk once the UI started auto-querying every discoverable project pod at login.
bugs.fix: Added GET /api/v1/user-roles/me (depends on get_current_user, no admin gate, returns {username, role}). Changed get_current_user's dev bypass condition to `settings.ENV == 'dev' and not settings.TAPIS_ENFORCE_AUTH_IN_DEV`, matching authenticate_user's existing skip_enforcement logic.

bugs.error_message: {"detail":"{\"result\":null,\"status\":\"error\",...\"message\":[\": Value error, No user has APPROVEDADMIN permission to configure CORS settings for networking object 'default', cors_allow_origins: [...]. Contact admin for approval.\"]...}"} when creating a new pod bundle via the Upstream UI Admin page
bugs.root_cause: Tapis Pods gates any write to networking.<key>.cors_allow_origins/methods/headers/credentials behind a separate APPROVEDADMIN permission tier (distinct from pod ADMIN/USER/READ) that can't be self-granted and must be approved by a real Tapis platform admin out-of-band. Commit 2c8932e (earlier this session) moved cors_allow_origins into build_bundle()'s create_pod() POST payload assuming the gate only applied to PUT-based edits of an existing pod, not initial creation. That assumption is false: create_pod() is called with the end user's own forwarded Tapis token (PodsService(token_override=tapis_token) in pods.py), which doesn't hold APPROVEDADMIN, so the entire bundle-creation POST now fails instead of just a later CORS PUT. grant_default_admin_permissions() only grants pod-level ADMIN, never APPROVEDADMIN, to DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERS.
bugs.fix: Reverted the cors_allow_origins/methods/headers/credentials fields out of build_bundle()'s create-time api_payload (pod creation now succeeds using the end user's token as before). Added PodsService._bootstrap_pod_cors(), run after API pod creation, using the service account's token (_fetch_service_token(), now live) to POST /v3/pods/{pod_id}/permissions self-granting APPROVEDADMIN (confirmed per-pod scoped, and confirmed the user authorized this self-approval), then PUT /v3/pods/{pod_id} with the CORS config. Best-effort: any failure is logged and returned as {status: pending_manual_approval, error}, never raised, so bundle creation still succeeds. cors_status surfaced in the POST /api/v1/pods/bundle response. Security-reviewed before implementation (flagged scope/intent as blocking unknowns, both resolved by user before coding). 139/139 backend tests pass.

bugs.error_message: {"detail":"{...\"message\":\"Got IntegrityError - psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation : Key (pod_id)=(snifferpostgres) already exists.\"...}"} when retrying pod bundle creation via the Admin UI with a base name used in an earlier partial/failed attempt
bugs.root_cause: create_stack() and create_volume() both already treat 'already exists'/'uniqueviolation' as success so bundle creation is idempotent, but create_pod() only special-cased specific volume_mounts payload-shape errors — any pre-existing pod_id (e.g. left over from an earlier attempt that failed partway through, such as the bug-002 CORS failure) caused create_pod() to raise, which pods.py's generic except Exception turned into a raw 502 with the Postgres IntegrityError text.
bugs.fix: create_pod() now checks for 'already exists'/'uniqueviolation' in the error message (case-insensitive) before its volume_mounts-specific checks, and returns {status: 'exists', pod_id} instead of raising, mirroring create_stack()/create_volume()'s existing pattern.

bugs.error_message: sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg.errors.DuplicateObject) type "note_scope" already exists — CREATE TYPE note_scope AS ENUM (...) — raised during `alembic upgrade heads` on pod startup, blocking the startup retry loop permanently
bugs.root_cause: upgrade() issued a raw `op.execute("CREATE TYPE note_scope AS ENUM (...)")` AND declared the notes.scope column as `sa.Enum(..., name="note_scope")` inside the same create_table() call. sa.Enum's own DDL also emits CREATE TYPE as part of create_table, so both statements ran in the same transaction and Postgres rejected the second as a duplicate — deterministic on every fresh database, not an environment fluke. Since pod startup runs `until alembic upgrade heads; do ...; sleep 10; done`, this wedged startup in an infinite retry loop that could never succeed.
bugs.fix: Removed the redundant raw CREATE TYPE statement; sa.Enum(...) inside create_table() already creates the type correctly on its own. Verified end-to-end against a fresh postgis/postgis:17-3.5 container: `alembic upgrade heads` now completes, and \d notes / \dT+ note_scope show the expected schema including the later 'sensor' enum value/column from b2c3d4e5f6a7.

bugs.error_message: {"detail":"{...\"message\":\"Not authorized -- you do not have access to this endpoint. POST /pods/{pod_id}/permissions\"...}"} when creating a pod bundle via the Admin UI
bugs.root_cause: build_bundle() called _bootstrap_pod_cors() (bug-002's fix) BEFORE grant_default_admin_permissions(). _bootstrap_pod_cors uses the service account's token to self-grant APPROVEDADMIN on the brand-new pod, but the service account has zero existing permission on a pod it didn't create — Tapis rejects POST /pods/{pod_id}/permissions from a caller with no prior access at all, a stricter check than just missing APPROVEDADMIN. The service account (tasclient_dsso) IS in DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERS, but grant_default_admin_permissions() — which grants it ADMIN using the pod-creating user's own authoritative token — ran AFTER the CORS bootstrap, too late to help.
bugs.fix: Swapped the order in build_bundle(): grant_default_admin_permissions() now runs before _bootstrap_pod_cors(), so the service account has baseline ADMIN access before attempting to self-elevate to APPROVEDADMIN. Added test_build_bundle_grants_admin_permissions_before_cors_bootstrap to lock in the ordering. SUPERSEDED (2026-07-22): the same 'Not authorized' error persisted even with correct ordering, confirmed logged-in user (wmobley) and confirmed service username (tasclient_dsso) both matching assumptions. Root cause never fully confirmed. Per user decision, the whole APPROVEDADMIN self-elevation approach was abandoned rather than debugged further — see bug-006.

bugs.error_message: Not a bug fix — user decision to abandon the automated CORS/APPROVEDADMIN bootstrap (bug-002 through bug-005) after repeated attempts (create-payload baking, service-account self-grant, ordering fix) all failed to resolve 'Not authorized -- you do not have access to this endpoint' on POST /pods/{pod_id}/permissions.
bugs.root_cause: N/A — root cause of the underlying Tapis 'Not authorized' rejection was never conclusively identified despite ruling out create-vs-edit timing (bug-002), grant ordering (bug-005), tenant id (confirmed correct), and identity (confirmed wmobley/tasclient_dsso as expected). Continuing to debug blind against live Tapis behavior with no direct access to inspect the platform's own authorization logs was unproductive.
bugs.fix: Removed _bootstrap_pod_cors(), _fetch_service_token(), the token-override plumbing in _headers()/_request(), and the ui_origin/api_cors_config construction entirely from build_bundle(). CORS configuration and the APPROVEDADMIN grant it requires are now purely manual/out-of-band (via update_cors_all.py, update_cors.py, or direct Tapis admin action) — build_bundle() only creates pods and grants ADMIN (not APPROVEDADMIN) via grant_default_admin_permissions(), which is unaffected and stays.

bugs.error_message: sqlalchemy.exc.DataError: (psycopg.errors.InvalidTextRepresentation) invalid input value for enum note_scope: "CAMPAIGN" / "STATION" on GET /campaigns/{id}/notes and /campaigns/{id}/stations/{id}/notes
bugs.root_cause: Note.scope is declared as SAEnum(NoteScope, name="note_scope") with no values_callable. SQLAlchemy's default binding for a PEP-435 enum class uses the member's .name (e.g. "CAMPAIGN"), not .value (e.g. "campaign"). The actual Postgres enum type (created by migrations a1b2c3d4e5f6/b2c3d4e5f6a7) only contains the lowercase .value strings. Every filter/insert against notes.scope sent the uppercase name, which Postgres rejected.
bugs.fix: Added values_callable=lambda enum: [e.value for e in enum] to the SAEnum column definition so SQLAlchemy binds/reads the lowercase .value strings matching the DB enum labels.

bugs.error_message: CI mypy step failing: examples/upload_and_annotate_demo.py:29-32: error: Cannot find implementation or library stub for module named "upstream", "upstream.exceptions", "upstream_api_client.models.campaigns_in", "upstream_api_client.models.station_create"  [import-not-found]
bugs.root_cause: mypy.ini scopes files to app but sets exclude only for alembic/tests/scripts/app.pytas; CI runs "mypy ." (whole repo) which still walks examples/, a new directory added for a standalone demo script that imports the external upstream-sdk package (upstream, upstream_api_client) which is not installed as a project dependency.
bugs.fix: Added ^examples/ to the exclude regex in mypy.ini, matching how scripts/ and tests/ are already excluded from strict type-checking since they are not part of the app package.
